action: Evening review: Recall one moment related to this idea. Tomorrow, share a work of art and ask what another person experiences in it.

author: Jesus of Nazareth
text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
action: With another person: Notice where your attention goes when you make a choice. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: David Hume
source: An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding, Section XII
text: A wise man, therefore, proportions his belief to the evidence.
action: With another person: Examine what evidence supports an opinion you hold. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Louis Pasteur
source: Lecture at University of Lille (1854; English translation)
text: In the fields of observation chance favors only the prepared mind.
action: Morning practice: Write one sentence about this idea, then use a tool to support thinking rather than replace it.

author: William Shakespeare
text: There is nothing either good or bad, but thinking makes it so.
action: Today's small experiment: Notice how a change in viewpoint alters your interpretation. In your journal, distinguish what you observed from what you inferred.

author: Paul the Apostle
text: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.
action: With another person: Offer kindness without expecting recognition. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Immanuel Kant
source: An Answer to the Question: What Is Enlightenment? (English translation)
text: Dare to know!
action: With another person: Investigate a question rather than avoiding uncertainty. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Ada Lovelace
text: The Analytical Engine has no pretensions whatever to originate anything.
action: Morning practice: Write one sentence about this idea, then look for a pattern, then ask what evidence would disprove it.

author: William Shakespeare
source: The Tempest, Act IV, Scene I
text: We are such stuff as dreams are made on.
action: Today's small experiment: Let a playful perspective loosen a rigid judgment. In your journal, distinguish what you observed from what you inferred.

author: Hebrew Bible
text: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.
action: With another person: Allow a change of plans without treating it as a failure. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Mary Wollstonecraft
source: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792)
text: I do not wish them to have power over men; but over themselves.
action: With another person: Act independently in a way that respects others. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Galileo Galilei
text: The universe ... is written in the language of mathematics.
action: Morning practice: Write one sentence about this idea, then consider one way a machine or system differs from a person.

author: William Shakespeare
source: As You Like It, Act II, Scene VII
text: All the world’s a stage.
action: Today's small experiment: Notice the roles you play without mistaking them for your whole identity. In your journal, distinguish what you observed from what you inferred.

author: Hebrew Bible
text: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
action: With another person: Respond gently when you disagree. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Henry David Thoreau
source: Walden, “Where I Lived, and What I Lived For”
text: Our life is frittered away by detail. Simplify, simplify.
action: With another person: Remove one unnecessary demand from your schedule. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Isaac Newton
text: If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of Giants.
action: During a conversation: Acknowledge someone whose work has helped yours.

author: William Blake
text: To see a World in a Grain of Sand.
action: Today's small experiment: Observe the ordinary world as if seeing it for the first time. In your journal, distinguish what you observed from what you inferred.

author: Hebrew Bible
text: What doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?
action: With another person: Choose one fair action even when it is inconvenient. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
text: Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.
action: With another person: Choose one action that expresses your considered values. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Isaac Newton
text: I frame no hypotheses.
action: During a conversation: Test an explanation against a counterexample.

author: William Blake
source: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
text: If the doors of perception were cleansed every thing would appear to man as it is, infinite.
action: Today's small experiment: Question one habitual perception. In your journal, distinguish what you observed from what you inferred.

author: Qur’an
text: There is no compulsion in religion.
action: With another person: Respect someone's freedom to believe differently. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Friedrich Nietzsche
source: Twilight of the Idols, “Maxims and Arrows” 8 (English translation)
text: What does not kill me makes me stronger.
action: With another person: Reflect on a difficulty and what it taught you, without glorifying suffering. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Charles Darwin
text: Ignorance more frequently begets confidence than does knowledge.
action: During a conversation: Admit one thing you do not yet know.

author: John Keats
text: Beauty is truth, truth beauty.
action: Today's small experiment: Look for beauty without claiming to possess it. In your journal, distinguish what you observed from what you inferred.

author: Qur’an
text: With hardship comes ease.
action: With another person: When something is difficult, identify one possible next step. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Bertrand Russell
source: The Problems of Philosophy (1912), concluding chapter
text: Philosophy is to be studied, not for the sake of any definite answers to its questions.
action: With another person: Sit with an unanswered question for five minutes. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Charles Darwin
text: There is grandeur in this view of life.
action: During a conversation: Notice one pattern in nature and ask how it works.

author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
text: Poets are the unacknowledged legislators of the world.
action: Today's small experiment: Read a poem slowly and consider what it leaves unsaid. In your journal, distinguish what you observed from what you inferred.

author: Qur’an
text: We made you into nations and tribes so that you may know one another.
action: With another person: Learn one thing from someone whose background differs from yours. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Socrates (as portrayed by Plato)
text: The unexamined life is not worth living.
action: Evening review: Recall one moment related to this idea. Tomorrow, question an assumption you have not examined.

author: Michael Faraday
text: Nothing is too wonderful to be true, if it be consistent with the laws of nature.
action: During a conversation: Prepare carefully for a small opportunity.

author: Emily Dickinson
text: Tell all the truth but tell it slant —
action: Today's small experiment: Express one difficult truth with care. In your journal, distinguish what you observed from what you inferred.

author: Dhammapada
text: Hatred is never appeased by hatred in this world. By non-hatred alone is hatred appeased.
action: With another person: Notice resentment without feeding it. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Aristotle
source: Metaphysics, Book I (English rendering; translations vary)
text: All men by nature desire to know.
action: Evening review: Recall one moment related to this idea. Tomorrow, read one unfamiliar perspective with curiosity.

author: Louis Pasteur
source: Lecture at University of Lille (1854; English translation)
text: In the fields of observation chance favors only the prepared mind.
action: During a conversation: Use a tool to support thinking rather than replace it.

author: Walt Whitman
text: I contain multitudes.
action: Today's small experiment: Hold two apparently conflicting feelings without rushing to resolve them. In your journal, distinguish what you observed from what you inferred.

author: Dhammapada
text: To avoid all evil, to cultivate good, and to cleanse one’s mind—this is the teaching of the Buddhas.
action: With another person: Replace one harmful habit with a helpful one. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Epictetus
text: Some things are in our control and others not.
action: Evening review: Recall one moment related to this idea. Tomorrow, separate what you can influence from what you cannot.

author: Ada Lovelace
text: The Analytical Engine has no pretensions whatever to originate anything.
action: During a conversation: Look for a pattern, then ask what evidence would disprove it.

author: Oscar Wilde
source: The Picture of Dorian Gray, Preface
text: All art is quite useless.
action: Today's small experiment: Make something small purely for the joy of creating. In your journal, distinguish what you observed from what you inferred.

author: Laozi
source: Tao Te Ching, chapter 1 (English rendering; translations vary)
text: The Tao that can be told is not the eternal Tao.
action: With another person: Spend a minute observing before naming your experience. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Marcus Aurelius
text: Men seek retreats for themselves, houses in the country, sea-shores, and mountains.
action: Evening review: Recall one moment related to this idea. Tomorrow, take a short quiet pause in the middle of a busy day.

author: Galileo Galilei
text: The universe ... is written in the language of mathematics.
action: During a conversation: Consider one way a machine or system differs from a person.

action: Today's small experiment: Share a work of art and ask what another person experiences in it. In your journal, distinguish what you observed from what you inferred.

author: Laozi
source: Tao Te Ching, chapter 64 (English rendering; translations vary)
text: A journey of a thousand miles begins beneath one’s feet.
action: With another person: Begin one worthwhile task, however small. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: René Descartes
source: Discourse on the Method, Part IV (English translation)
text: I think, therefore I am.
action: Evening review: Recall one moment related to this idea. Tomorrow, describe one experience without immediately interpreting it.

author: William Shakespeare
text: There is nothing either good or bad, but thinking makes it so.
action: Just for today: Notice how a change in viewpoint alters your interpretation.

author: Bhagavad Gita
text: You have the right to work, but not to the fruits of work.
action: With another person: Do your work carefully without obsessing over praise. Respect their perspective and boundaries.

author: Francis Bacon
text: Knowledge is power.
action: Evening review: Recall one moment related to this idea. Tomorrow, write down a belief you would be willing to revise.

author: Isaac Newton
text: I frame no hypotheses.
action: Quiet reflection: Take two minutes to consider why this matters; then test an explanation against a counterexample.

author: William Shakespeare
source: The Tempest, Act IV, Scene I
text: We are such stuff as dreams are made on.
action: Just for today: Let a playful perspective loosen a rigid judgment.

author: Jesus of Nazareth
text: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find.
action: Evening review: Recall one moment related to this idea. Tomorrow, ask a sincere question and listen carefully to the answer.

author: John Locke
source: An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, Book II, chapter 1
text: Let us then suppose the mind to be, as we say, white paper, void of all characters.
action: Evening review: Recall one moment related to this idea. Tomorrow, learn one useful fact and share it responsibly.

author: Charles Darwin
text: Ignorance more frequently begets confidence than does knowledge.

source: As You Like It, Act II, Scene VII
text: All the world’s a stage.
action: Just for today: Notice the roles you play without mistaking them for your whole identity.

author: Jesus of Nazareth
text: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
action: Evening review: Recall one moment related to this idea. Tomorrow, do one small act that reduces conflict.
